issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a 'Milkable' interface (with method messageOnMilk()), and the template Main.java also references Milkable. However, the solution repository does not define or use a 'Milkable' interface: it instead defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (Dairy.java) and the classes Goat and Seal implement Dairy. Additionally, there is an empty Milkable.java file in the solution repository. This naming mismatch (Milkable vs. Dairy) and the empty Milkable.java are structural inconsistencies that will confuse students about which interface to implement and may cause tests or template references to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update its file name to Milkable.java with the same method signature String messageOnMilk()), and update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable. Remove the empty Milkable.java file or replace it with the proper interface. This ensures consistency with the problem statement, template references, and expected student implementations.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (the UML and example code expect Milkable.messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (Dairy.messageOnMilk()) and leaves Milkable.java empty. This renaming of the same conceptual interface across artifacts creates a mapping mismatch: students are asked to implement/use 'Milkable' but the reference solution and some implementation files use 'Dairy', causing confusion and extra work to reconcile names.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (or conversely rename all 'Milkable' references in problem/template to 'Dairy'), and ensure the Milkable.java in the solution contains the messageOnMilk() declaration. Update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable so the interface name matches the UML/problem statement and template usage.
